text:
Anya: Heads-up — saw a spike of OOMs and kernel fallbacks in the multi-model co-residency canary last night. Dumped a short perf slice. p99 latency and OOM rate both up ~3x for the slot with two large models.

Anya: flamegraph snippet (trimmed):
```
alloc_slab::evict  28%
kvcache::lookup  12%
kernel_selector::choose  10%
batcher::try_batch  9%
memcpy_async  8%
allocator::compact 5%
fallback_cublas_path 4%
```
Observation: frequent small slab evictions -> KV swap thrash -> kernel selector moves to fallback kernels with higher memory pressure.

Sam: Thanks. Did you capture workspace sizes and the sequence length mix? Could be batching heuristics mixing short and long sequences leading to oversized workspace reservations per step.

Anya: Yes — the tenant mix was one long-context model (16k) + one standard (4k). Router had been packing them together to hit throughput targets. Workspace histogram: many allocations at 90% of slab size, then a cascade of evictions.

Jorge: Likely root cause: hard slab partitioning + aggressive packer. Two failure modes we saw before: 1) fragmentation where min_workspace is too large for mixed batches, 2) on-evict we don't prewarm the KV for the incoming model so first requests trigger a big KV fetch. Both cause kernel fallback + memcopy stalls.

Jorge: Quick mitigations to try (config snippets):
```yaml
allocator:
  soft_reserve_pct: 8   # keep some headroom per-GPU for swap spikes
  min_workspace_per_slot: 64MB
batcher:
  sequence_grouping: by_model_size
  max_mixed_batch_ratio: 0.2  # limit mixing large+small
kvcache:
  prewarm_on_handoff: true
  prefetch_parallelism: 2
```

Anya: Ran a small canary with soft_reserve_pct=8 and prewarm_on_handoff=true. Results (30m):
- OOM count: dropped from 18 -> 2
- p50 latency: +4% (slightly up due to prefetch traffic)
- p99 latency: -27%
Notes: variance increased a bit during prefetch windows.

Infra-bot: perf-run: https://perf.internal/redwood/runs/29811  (contains full traces and kernel traces) :chart_with_upwards_trend:

Luis: Good signal. Next steps I propose:
- allocator: implement proactive compaction on low-util ticks (opportunistic compaction, cheaply when gpu utilization < 30%)
- kvcache: prefetch-on-evict + metadata hints so router can request lighter batches during handoff
- batcher: add a "packing_hint" API so router can prefer homogeneous batches for co-residency slots
- telemetry: add trace events for "kvcache_swap_start/end", "allocator_compact_start/end", and "kernel_fallback(reason)"

Luis: Example trace points we want:
```
TRACE_KV_SWAP_START(tenant_id, model, bytes)
TRACE_ALLOC_COMPACT_START(gpu_id, free_before, free_after)
TRACE_KERNEL_FALLBACK(gpu_id, chosen_kernel, fallback_kernel, reason)
```

Sam: LGTM. Please open a short RFC for prefetch-on-evict + packing_hint and a rollout playbook (canary -> 5% -> 25% -> 100%). Add experiments to measure extra memory traffic cost vs p99 improvement. Also add an eval to ensure output parity after kernel fallback improvements.

Anya: Will open RFC + PR for traces today. Assigning follow-ups: @Jorge allocator compaction prototype, @Luis router packing_hint API, @Sam will own rollout playbook.

Anya: Quick question — should the router keep model pairs pinned to the same slab partition (soft affinity) or rely on the allocator to isolate? Thoughts?

Jorge: I prefer soft affinity at router level for multi-model slots (router knows workload mix). Combined approach: soft affinity + allocator soft_reserve per-partition gives best isolation with minimal wasted space.

Sam: Agree. Add a small metric "affinity_mismatch_rate" to see how often router breaks affinity for latency/cost reasons.

Anya: Thanks all — I'll post RFC link when created. :thumbsup:
